blogPosts.title: How Much Does a Commercial Fitout Cost in Southbank in 2026?
blogPosts.excerpt: A detailed breakdown of commercial fitout costs in Southbank, including office, retail, and hospitality spaces. Get realistic budgets and tips to save.
body: If you're planning a commercial fitout in Southbank in 2026, one of the first questions you'll ask is 'how much will it cost?' The answer depends on several factors including the size of your space, the level of finish, and whether you need structural changes. In this guide, we break down typical costs for office, retail, and hospitality fitouts in Southbank and surrounding suburbs.

For a basic office fitout in Southbank, you can expect to pay between $800 and $1,500 per square metre. This includes partitioning, basic electrical and data cabling, painting, and carpet. If you want a higher-end finish with feature walls, premium joinery, and end-of-trip facilities, the cost can rise to $2,500 per square metre or more. Retail fitouts vary widely depending on the brand and fixtures required.

One of the biggest cost drivers is the condition of the existing shell. A bare shell fitout requires more work — new ceilings, HVAC, fire services, and floor coverings — which adds to the budget. Conversely, a refurbishment of an existing tenancy can be more cost-effective. Always factor in a contingency of 10-15% for unforeseen issues like asbestos or structural surprises.

Council approvals and permits are another consideration. In Southbank, part of the City of Melbourne, you'll need a building permit and possibly a planning permit depending on the use. 8Projects handles all council liaison as part of our service, so you don't have to worry about the paperwork. We also ensure compliance with the National Construction Code and Australian Standards.

Timing also affects cost. If you need a fast-tracked fitout, you may pay a premium for overtime labour and expedited material orders. A typical commercial fitout in Southbank takes 8 to 16 weeks from start to finish, depending on complexity. Planning ahead and locking in your design early can save both time and money.

To get an accurate quote for your Southbank commercial fitout, contact 8Projects for a free on-site consultation. We'll assess your space, discuss your requirements, and provide a fixed-price quote with no hidden fees. Our team has completed fitouts for offices, retail stores, and hospitality venues across Melbourne, and we know how to deliver on time and on budget.

blogPosts.title: Top 5 Things to Consider Before Building a Custom Home in South Melbourne
blogPosts.excerpt: Thinking of building a custom home in South Melbourne? Here are five crucial factors including heritage overlays, council rules, and choosing the right builder.
body: Building a custom home in South Melbourne is an exciting journey, but it comes with unique challenges. The area is known for its heritage streetscapes, narrow blocks, and strict council regulations. Before you break ground, there are five key things every homeowner should consider to ensure a smooth build and a stunning result.

First, understand the heritage overlay. Many parts of South Melbourne are covered by heritage controls that restrict what you can do to the exterior of your home. You may need a planning permit for even minor changes like new windows or cladding. Working with a builder who has experience in heritage projects, like 8Projects, can save you months of delays.

Second, get your finances in order early. Custom homes in South Melbourne typically cost between $2,500 and $4,000 per square metre, depending on finishes and complexity. Factor in costs for architect fees, engineering, permits, and landscaping. A fixed-price contract from your builder gives you certainty and protects against cost blowouts.

Third, choose the right block. South Melbourne has many narrow lots and laneway access points. Check the site for easements, soil conditions, and existing services. A geotechnical report is essential to avoid surprises during excavation. Your builder can coordinate this as part of the pre-construction phase.

Fourth, design for the climate. Melbourne's weather is famously changeable, so consider passive solar design, good insulation, and cross-ventilation. Double-glazed windows and thermal mass materials like concrete floors can reduce energy bills and keep your home comfortable year-round. Sustainable design is also increasingly valued by buyers.

Finally, pick a builder with local knowledge. 8Projects has completed multiple custom homes in South Melbourne and knows the council's expectations. We'll guide you through the permit process, recommend trusted architects, and deliver a home that's built to last. Contact us for a free consultation to discuss your dream home.

blogPosts.title: Retail Shop Fitout Guide for Melbourne's CBD: Permits, Costs & Timeline
blogPosts.excerpt: Opening a retail store in Melbourne's CBD? This guide covers everything from permits and costs to fitout timelines, with tips from 8Projects' experienced team.
body: Melbourne's CBD is one of Australia's most competitive retail markets. A successful shop fitout can make the difference between a store that draws customers in and one that gets overlooked. Whether you're opening a boutique, a cafe, or a flagship store, understanding the process is critical. This guide walks you through permits, costs, and timelines for a retail fitout in the CBD.

The first step is securing the right permits. In the City of Melbourne, you'll need a building permit for most fitout works, and possibly a planning permit if you're changing the use of the space. Signage also requires a separate permit. 8Projects manages all permit applications on your behalf, ensuring compliance with the Building Act 1993 and local laws.

Costs for a retail fitout in Melbourne's CBD typically range from $1,200 to $3,000 per square metre. A basic fitout with off-the-shelf shelving, standard lighting, and vinyl flooring is at the lower end. A high-end fitout with custom joinery, feature lighting, and premium finishes can exceed $4,000 per square metre. Always include a contingency for heritage requirements if your shop is in a heritage building.

Timeline is another critical factor. A straightforward retail fitout in the CBD can take 6 to 10 weeks from permit approval to completion. However, if your space requires structural changes, new HVAC, or fire services, expect 12 to 16 weeks. 8Projects provides a detailed project schedule upfront so you can plan your opening date with confidence.

One often-overlooked aspect is the importance of traffic flow and customer experience. Your fitout should guide customers naturally through the space, highlight key products, and create an inviting atmosphere. Good lighting, clear signage, and durable finishes are essential for high-traffic retail environments. We work with designers to optimise your layout for both aesthetics and function.

Ready to start your retail fitout in Melbourne's CBD? Contact 8Projects for a free on-site consultation. We'll discuss your vision, provide a fixed-price quote, and handle the entire fitout process from permits to handover. Our team has delivered retail spaces for brands across Melbourne, and we're ready to help you succeed.

blogPosts.title: Office Renovation vs New Build: Which Is Right for Your Southbank Business?
blogPosts.excerpt: Should you renovate your existing Southbank office or build new? Compare costs, timelines, and benefits with insights from 8Projects' commercial construction experts.
body: Southbank is home to a thriving business community, and many companies face the decision of whether to renovate their current office space or build a new one from scratch. Both options have their pros and cons, and the right choice depends on your budget, timeline, and long-term goals. In this article, we compare office renovation versus new build for Southbank businesses.

Renovating an existing office is often faster and more cost-effective than building new. You can typically complete a renovation in 8 to 12 weeks, and costs are lower because the structure, services, and shell are already in place. Renovations are ideal if you're happy with your location but need to update the layout, finishes, or technology. However, you may be limited by the existing floor plan and services.

A new build office gives you complete control over the design, from the floor plate to the facade. You can optimise the layout for your workflow, incorporate the latest sustainable technologies, and create a space that truly reflects your brand. The downside is that new builds take longer — typically 12 to 18 months from concept to completion — and require a larger budget. They also involve more complex council approvals.

Cost is a major factor. In Southbank, office renovation costs range from $1,000 to $2,000 per square metre, while a new build can cost $3,000 to $5,000 per square metre or more. However, a new build may offer better long-term value if you plan to stay in the space for 10+ years, as you can design for energy efficiency and future flexibility.

Another consideration is disruption to your business. Renovations can often be staged to allow you to remain operational, while a new build requires you to relocate temporarily. 8Projects specialises in minimising downtime during renovations, with after-hours work and careful phasing to keep your business running smoothly.

Ultimately, the best choice depends on your specific needs. 8Projects offers free consultations to discuss your Southbank office project. We'll assess your current space, understand your goals, and provide expert advice on whether renovation or new build is the right path. Contact us today to start the conversation.
